page.layout: One page of text, centred verse. Top: two-line verse stanza under the running head. Then a head and a poem of ten lines, a second head and a poem of ten stanzas, and the catchword at the right foot. No margin notes. Show-through from the reverse is not transcribed.

p.i: Nunc igitur cœlum invenì sedesq; beatas, Moxq; suam inveniet Brentius Utopiam.

Gratulor ipse tibi cūm mundum conspicor istum Martyr, quod saluum te Deus eripuit. Rursum ubi doctrinæ Christi considero sortem, Ad gemitum & luctum me tua fata vocant. Quidquid id est, pro te sit semper gloria Christo, Namq; ut sis Martyr & Petrus ipse dedit. Ut Martyr de Christo es testificatus aperte, Et probat esse Petrum te tua firma fides. Ingressus sedem cœli es non ἀτοπικῶς[?], sed Sanctorum quæ sit commoda spiritibus.

Ergo ego chare senex nobis te propter ademptum Cogor in æterna vivere tristitia? Ergo ego vicinus frustra tibi factus, ut acri Pro lætis studijs carpar amaritie? Vidi ego complures doctos, vaga flumina mittunt Qua sua Ticinus, Sequana, Danubius, Vidi ego, sed nullum, te præter, (parcite docti) Quem vere potui dicere doctiloquum. Tu mihi solus eras, in summo limine vitæ, (Nam binis annis te fueram senior) Cuius honorandæ voces oracla fuere, Certa pij & docti pectoris indicia. Nunc quibus orbato mihi spes hæc unica restat, Mox simul in cœlis me fore, te socio.

page.notes: Right margin shows only show-through from the reverse side, not transcribed. Faint "34" at the lower centre is show-through, not a page number. The Greek word after "non" is hard to read and is marked [?]. The abbreviation "Moxq;" and "sedesq;" are read from the scan. The "VV" in the first head is printed as two V's and kept as printed.
